title: Bihar Removes Khagaria SP Bhanu Pratap Singh Amid Wife's Complaints
excerpt: The 2021-batch IPS officer has been attached to Patna headquarters in a five-officer reshuffle, after weeks of public complaints by his wife — allegations that remain untested by any inquiry.
body:
• The Bihar government has removed Khagaria Superintendent of Police Bhanu Pratap Singh from his post and directed him to report to police headquarters in Patna with immediate effect, in a November 4 reshuffle of five IPS officers.
  • Shailendra Singh, previously SP of Sheohar, takes charge in Khagaria.
  • The transfer follows complaints and protests by the officer's wife, Pooja Singh, who has alleged mistreatment and being kept from the couple's young daughter. The allegations have not been established by any investigation or court finding, and no response from the officer was reported in the latest coverage.
  • The Bihar State Women Commission summoned the officer on October 26; in October, his wife told reporters she did not want a divorce and hoped the couple could reconcile.

The Bihar government has removed Bhanu Pratap Singh, a 2021-batch IPS officer, as Superintendent of Police of Khagaria and attached him to the Bihar Police Headquarters in Patna with immediate effect. The order came on Wednesday, November 4, as part of a Home Department reshuffle transferring five IPS officers, IANS reported. Shailendra Singh, who was SP of Sheohar, has been appointed the new SP of Khagaria. Singh has been placed at headquarters pending a fresh posting.

The complaints behind the transfer

The Home Department notification did not give a reason for Singh's removal, but he had recently been in the news following a public dispute with his wife. According to ReportWire's account of her complaints, Pooja Singh submitted a written application to the Gardanibagh Women Police Station in Patna alleging mistreatment by her husband and members of his family, pressure to sign divorce papers, and that the couple's young daughter has been kept away from her. She has also protested publicly in recent days seeking access to her daughter. These are allegations made by the complainant; they have not been tested by an investigation or a court, and the reports of the transfer carried no response from Singh.

How the dispute reached this point

The dispute has been building for weeks. The Bihar State Women Commission summoned the officer on October 26 after taking cognisance of his wife's complaint. In mid-October, Pooja Singh met Bihar DGP Preeta Verma to present her side — and told reporters afterwards that she did not want a divorce, hoped to reconcile, and did not want the dispute to damage her husband's career, describing him as an honest officer. Reports of the couple's dispute first emerged in September, when she approached police in Bharatpur, Rajasthan, where the officer's family lives. The couple married in 2017, before Singh entered the Indian Police Service in the 2021 batch.

What a headquarters attachment means

Attaching a district police chief to headquarters — removing him from command without a new posting — is the state government's standard instrument when an officer's continuance in a district post becomes untenable, whether for administrative, political or personal-controversy reasons. It is not a suspension and carries no finding of misconduct. Singh remains a serving IPS officer awaiting a posting decision, while the family dispute itself now sits with the Women Commission and the Patna women police station process his wife has set in motion. What either process concludes will determine whether this episode ends as a transfer or becomes a longer professional reckoning.
nri_angle: A district police chief's removal over a family dispute is a governance story about how personal controversies are handled inside India's police leadership.
